title: GPU commitment checklist — 1:1 prep (scratch)
content:
Quick personal prep for 1:1 with Priya — focused on Dedicated GPU commitments and short-term autoscale adjustments. This is a scratchpad, messy. Use sections as prompts.

Meeting goals:
- Get alignment on whether we should convert short-term burst (spot-like) to reserved for Q2 launch.
- Decide on concrete autoscaling policy tweaks to handle expected traffic surge from Feature X.
- Agree owner and timeline for the capacity-load test.

Key context (current state):
- Current Dedicated pool: 38 x A100-80GB reserved. Effective usable after headroom and fault isolation = 34.
- Average sustained throughput last 30d (all models): 1.2M tokens/day, peak day = 1.9M tokens.
- Avg pool utilization (rolling 7d): 68% during business hours, 52% nights.
- Recent deploy of chat-opt model increased soft-latency CPU work; observed 12% higher per-token compute.

Forecast assumptions (Q2 expected changes):
- Feature X (beta to 5% of sessions -> release to 50%) predicted +25% requests to hosted/dedicated split. Conservative cap: +15% baseline, optimistic +30%.
- New enterprise customer onboarding (deal S: committed 8 GPUs for 24/7). Start date mid-April.

Quick numbers (hand math):
- Baseline headroom plan (target 70% avg util): with +15% traffic, required GPUs = ceil( current_GPU_count * 1.15 * 0.68/0.70 ) ~ 40 GPUs (rounded). So +2 GPUs to keep same tail latency profile.
- Optimistic surge (+30%): target GPUs -> ~44 GPUs.
- Conservative reserved ask: +4 GPUs for April-June trial (buy 42 total), keep option to burst +10 via shared burst pool.

Policy suggestions to propose:
1) Reservations: commit to 42 GPUs for Q2 with monthly review. Rationale: small incremental commit keeps unit cost low w/o huge overcommit.
2) Autoscale tuning: target_utilization 65-75% (keep 70% center), scale_step = 2 GPUs for small oscillations, scale_step = 6 GPUs for sustained >10m overshoot, cool_down = 90s for downscale, 30s for upscale.
3) Burst capacity: reserve 10% of capacity as "burst headroom" (automatically preemptible to reduce cold-starts), specifically earmark for latency-critical routes (chat-streaming).
4) Model routing fallback: route long-context LLM requests to quantized v2 where acceptable (2x throughput gain) — requires update to smart routing policy.

Risk & tradeoffs to surface in 1:1:
- Cost: adding 4 reserved GPUs increases monthly commitment by ~ $Xk (need exact pricing from finance). Benefit: reduces 99th pct latency risk and avoids reactive preemptions.
- Over-reserving: if Feature X underperforms, we pay unused capacity; mitigations: short-term (3mo) commit + early termination clause or shift to Dedicated burst credits.
- Autoscale churn: too-aggressive step sizes -> oscillation causing headroom thrash and jitter in latency.

Action items to propose / follow up (assignable):
- A: Open infra load-test ticket to emulate +15% and +30% traffic patterns (owner: Tom) — due 2026-03-17.
- B: Run cost delta calc with finance for +2, +4, +6 GPUs (owner: me) — due 2026-03-12 (urgent before pricing call).
- C: Draft canary rollout config that pins 10% traffic to quantized v2 for long-context models (owner: Ellen) — due 2026-03-22.
- D: Add metric to console: burst-utilization-per-route and prewarm-miss-rate (owner: SRE) — ticket JIRA-ENG-SRE-391.

Questions I want to ask Priya / items to get buy-in on:
- Is leadership comfortable with a 3-month incremental reservation vs. pushing risk to burst credits? (cost tolerance)
- Preference on autoscale aggressiveness: prioritize latency SLOs or keep cost down? If latency, approve wider scale_step and larger reserved headroom.
- Can we add a contractual clause for early reduction of reserved pool if utilization < 40% for consecutive 30 days?

Notes / heuristics I want to remember to mention:
- For latency-critical routes, a miss in prefix cache is significantly costlier than compute — prewarming and targeted caching can be cheaper than adding GPUs.
- Quantization for medium-length requests (<=2048 tokens) is low-risk; longer contexts still need full precision testing.
- Autoscale cooldowns interact badly with baseline traffic waves (12:00-14:00). Avoid downscaling in the middle of the wave.

Scratch TODOs (personal):
- Pull detailed per-model per-route token counts for last 60 days (query bigquery).
- Check Dedicated pricing tiers doc for Q2 promo codes.
- Prepare short slide: "Why +4 now, +10 later" for sync with finance (1 slide, 3 bullets).

Random stray ideas (not for meeting unless Priya asks):
- Consider a mixed-instance pool: keep heavy models on A100-80, offload small embedding models to 1/2 A10G or 1x 40GB instances with aggressive quantization. Could save ~18% if we can isolate routing.
- Experiment: pre-warm twice at the start of business hours and after any large deploys; measure 95th latency delta.

End of scratchpad. Will tidy after 1:1 and turn into tidy follow-ups in shared_drives/engineering/dedicated/ if we make decisions.
